ending.reason: Sauti closes the scene ("The son of Gavalgana having in this manner administered comfort to the royal Dhritarashtra... then restored his mind to peace. Taking these facts for his subject, Dwaipayana composed a holy Upanishad"). It is the end of the Dhritarashtra–Sanjaya dialogue and a narration boundary. ¶41 turns to the merits of reading the Bharata.

segments.label: The fruit of the tree: the story in brief
segments.note: Vyasa fathers the three princes; how the Bharata was compiled and handed down; Pandu's misfortune and the birth of the Pandavas; their welcome at Hastinapura; Draupadi; Indraprastha, the Rajasuya and Duryodhana's envy; the dice and the war.

segments.label: Dhritarashtra's lament
segments.note: The blind king to Sanjaya: his self-justification (¶31), then 'When I heard..., then, O Sanjaya, I had no hope of success' through every turn of the story and the war (¶32–33), 'Alas!' (¶34–35); he faints (¶36).

segments.label: Sanjaya consoles the king
segments.note: Dhritarashtra wishes to die (¶37); Sanjaya recounts the great kings of old who also died, and the power of Time (¶38–39); Sauti closes the scene (¶40).

lines.text: Dhritarashtra, bewailing his fate in these words, was overcome with extreme anguish and for a time deprived of sense; but being revived, he addressed Sanjaya in the following words.

lines.text: The wise son of Gavalgana (Sanjaya) then addressed the distressed lord of Earth while thus talking and bewailing, sighing like a serpent and repeatedly tainting, in words of deep import.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Thou hast heard, O Raja, of the greatly powerful men of vast exertions, spoken of by Vyasa and the wise Narada; men born of great royal families, resplendent with worthy qualities, versed in the science of celestial arms, and in glory emblems of Indra; men who having conquered the world by justice and performed sacrifices with fit offerings (to the Brahmanas), obtained renown in this world and at last succumbed to the sway of time.

lines.text: Such were Saivya; the valiant Maharatha; Srinjaya, great amongst conquerors.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Besides these, other Rajas had gone before, still more powerful than they, mighty charioteers noble in mind, and resplendent with every worthy quality.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: These, O chief, and other Rajas, we hear enumerated by hundreds and by thousands, and still others by millions, princes of great power and wisdom, quitting very abundant enjoyments met death as thy sons have done!

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Their heavenly deeds, valour, and generosity, their magnanimity, faith, truth, purity, simplicity and mercy, are published to the world in the records of former times by sacred bards of great learning.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Though endued with every noble virtue, these have yielded up their lives.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Thy sons were malevolent, inflamed with passion, avaricious, and of very evil-disposition.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Thou art versed in the Sastras, O Bharata, and art intelligent and wise; they never sink under misfortunes whose understandings are guided by the Sastras.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Thou art acquainted, O prince, with the lenity and severity of fate; this anxiety therefore for the safety of thy children is unbecoming.
lines.tts_text: Thou art acquainted, O prince, with the lenity and severity of fate; this anxiety therefore for the safety of thy children is unbecoming.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Moreover, it behoveth thee not to grieve for that which must happen: for who can avert, by his wisdom, the decrees of fate?

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: No one can leave the way marked out for him by Providence.
lines.tts_text: No one can leave the way marked out for him by Providence.
lines.direction: a wise minister consoling a grieving king: steady, compassionate, unhurried

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Existence and non-existence, pleasure and pain all have Time for their root.
lines.tts_text: Existence and non-existence, pleasure and pain all have Time for their root.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Time createth all things and Time destroyeth all creatures.
lines.tts_text: Time createth all things and Time destroyeth all creatures.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: It is Time that burneth creatures and it is Time that extinguisheth the fire.
lines.tts_text: It is Time that burneth creatures and it is Time that extinguisheth the fire.
lines.direction: a wise minister consoling a grieving king: steady, compassionate, unhurried

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: All states, the good and the evil, in the three worlds, are caused by Time.
lines.tts_text: All states, the good and the evil, in the three worlds, are caused by Time.
lines.direction: a wise minister consoling a grieving king: steady, compassionate, unhurried

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Time cutteth short all things and createth them anew.
lines.tts_text: Time cutteth short all things and createth them anew.
lines.direction: a wise minister consoling a grieving king: steady, compassionate, unhurried

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Time alone is awake when all things are asleep: indeed, Time is incapable of being overcome.
lines.tts_text: Time alone is awake when all things are asleep: indeed, Time is incapable of being overcome.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Time passeth over all things without being retarded.
lines.tts_text: Time passeth over all things without being retarded.

lines.speaker: sanjaya
lines.text: Knowing, as thou dost, that all things past and future and all that exist at the present moment, are the offspring of Time, it behoveth thee not to throw away thy reason.
